answer: Witness co-signing rounds: each identity must collect signatures from peers who each expose a random challenge phrase (quill, mesa, sonnet) tied to their own history. Duplicate identities fail because a fresh clone cannot supply witnesses with independent, verifiable histories, so copying evidence reveals correlated origins. An attacker pays the full cost of maintaining separate interaction records per clone, scaling linearly with each identity, plus the risk that one leaked witness link exposes the whole cluster.
